HELLO FILO NUBDAOS! ⭐

​We are finally sharing the official Fan VCR played during #TheWickedGameFMinManila. 🎞️

​To everyone who sent video messages and took the time to film, thank you for making this masterpiece possible. Seeing Daou and Offroad watch and appreciate every second made every bit of effort worth it. 🥹

​Our hearts are full hearing their response. Daou mentioned that after seeing the video, he has a new aim: he now knows exactly why he has to wake up and be happy every day. Offroad also shared how much he values our patience, knowing how long we waited for this moment, and how happy he is that we finally met. ✨

​To all the Filo Nubdaos who attended our fan events, thank you so much! It was so good to see everyone. I hope we can meet again soon, and mas dumami pa tayo sa next fan gatherings! 🫶🔥

​The wait was long, but seeing them was a dream come true. Here’s to seeing them again and again! 🤗

​To our donors and participants: our fan projects wouldn't happen without you. Let’s keep this fire burning for the next ones! 💙🧡

 OUROAD IN THE PHILIPPINES
​#DaouOffroad #Nubdao #TheWickedGameFMinManila

data.text:
In Memoriam
Ma. Julia “Jojo” Leachon-Balbuena
(November 19, 1958 – May 3, 2026)

As a physician, I never imagined that death could come so soon within our family. Though I have long embraced memento mori—the fragility of life and the acceptance that it must one day end—nothing prepares the heart for the loss of someone so dear.

It is with deep sorrow and pain that we announce the untimely passing of our beloved sister Jojo, the matriarch of the Leachon family, this May 3, 2026, in Calapan, Oriental Mindoro.

She was the light of every reunion—showering us with extraordinary love and kindness, spoiling us with gifts and food, and reminding us that family is the greatest treasure. After surviving the great Pasay fire of 1967, our family moved to Calapan, where Jojo finished her elementary and high school at Holy Infant Academy, later earning her BS Medical Technology degree at FEU. She was happily married to Engineer Joey Balbuena.

“But there’s a story behind everything… behind all your stories is always your mother’s story, because hers is where yours begin.”
— Mitch Albom, For One More Day

Together, Jojo and Joey were blessed with three loving children—Lawyer RJ, oncologist Dr. JM, and Engineer Chi—along with their kind spouses and wonderful grandchildren who brought her immense joy and pride. Jojo’s life was a testament to Albom’s words: she was not only a great sister, but also a hardworking mother whose devotion shaped the lives of her children and grandchildren.

Our proud parents, Judge Emilio Leachon and Pilar Cueto Leachon, raised us—siblings Marita (with her husband Kiko), Lito, Beck Beck, Archie, City Mayor Doy, and myself—with values of humility, service, and resilience. Jojo embodied these values fully. We shared childhood joys, college days, and milestones in later years, always bound by her quiet strength and devotion.

As Helen Keller beautifully said: “What we once enjoyed and deeply loved we can never lose, for all that we love deeply becomes a part of us.” Truly, Jojo was “a gift to the heart, a friend to the spirit, a golden thread to the meaning of life.”

Born on November 19, 1958, she lived a life of competence, compassion, and quiet strength. As the eldest sister and guiding light of our family, she embodied love and responsibility, always placing others before herself.

A devoted mother and grandmother, she labored tirelessly to raise successful children and nurture wonderful grandchildren, instilling in them the values of hard work, humility, and care. Her presence was a source of comfort and inspiration, and her absence leaves a void that words cannot fill.

She was caring, loving, and deeply committed to those around her. Truly, she was special.

We will miss her terribly.

Prayer
Eternal Father, we entrust Jojo into Your loving embrace. Grant her eternal rest and let perpetual light shine upon her. May her soul, through Your mercy, find peace, and may we, her family, be strengthened by the memory of her love, her devotion, and her quiet strength. Comfort us in our grief, and guide us to live with the same humility, compassion, and faith that she embodied. Amen.

— Dr. Tony Leachon
